rows.result: Each template has one dominant intent: collections = sell/browse a category, PDPs = sell a product, blog posts = educate/style. No purpose ambiguity.

Commercial category keywords (e.g. 'heels for women', 385k+ impr) map to category collection pages with product grids + intro copy — matches SERP intent. Blog informational queries map to blog posts. Confirmed against keywords/keywords.csv.

Priority collections carry descriptive intro copy (womens-heels ~149 words) plus product grids; PDPs have descriptions + customer reviews; blogs are in-depth. Note: many secondary/occasion and dated collections have little or no intro copy.
rows.next_action: Add 100-150 word intent-rich intros to priority collections that lack them (boots, mules, men's sandals) to support weak-ranking head terms.

rows.result: Primary keyword appears in title/H1/intro on category pages; meta descriptions carry secondaries (block, kitten, platform, wedge heels). No stuffing observed. Matches clusters in keywords/clusters.json.
Blog is active (20 tracked posts dated 2026-02 to 2026-07 of 89 total); collections are evergreen. Content is current.

Product-level E-E-A-T is strong (real Judge.me reviews + aggregateRating + 25-year brand legacy). However blog posts lack visible author bylines/credentials, weakening topical expertise signals for informational content.
rows.next_action: Add author bylines with short bios/expertise to blog posts; surface brand-legacy (since 1998) trust signals on category pages.

rows.result: Collections and PDPs contain multiple contextual internal links (nav categories, related products, breadcrumbs, blog cross-links). >=2 relevant links per page.
